statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-11822 is an out-of-bounds read in fts5LeafSeek() in the SQLite FTS5 extension: a crafted database with a malformed FTS5 leaf page makes an FTS5 MATCH query read past the page buffer. SQLite lists it as fixed in 3.53.2, together with CVE-2026-11824: https://sqlite.org/cves.html, https://sqlite.org/releaselog/3_53_2.html, and the CVE record lists versions before 3.53.2 as affected: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-11822. Alpine lists CVE-2026-11822 as fixed in sqlite 3.53.4-r0 in the secfixes of Alpine's APKBUILD for sqlite 3.53.4-r0, from which the 3.53.4 builds are made: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/b45fc81206707171f23602615ce5619166014323/main/sqlite/APKBUILD. FTS5 is compiled in: the compile-option list in the shell and both libraries of every build includes ENABLE_FTS5. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes packages built from source sqlite (sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static, sqlite-dev and sqlite-doc) at 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0, 3.53.4-r0 and 3.53.4-r1, for x86_64 and aarch64. SQLite is compiled into three files in each build: the sqlite3 shell in the sqlite package, which carries its own copy and does not link libsqlite3; the shared library in sqlite-libs; and the static archive libsqlite3.a in sqlite-static. The shell and both libraries report SQLite 3.51.1 in the 3.51.1-r0 build, 3.51.2 in 3.51.2-r0, and 3.53.4 in 3.53.4-r0 and 3.53.4-r1, on both architectures. So 3.51.1-r0 and 3.51.2-r0, which are older than 3.53.2, are affected, and 3.53.4-r0 and later carry the fix.

CVE-2026-11822 is an out-of-bounds read in fts5LeafSeek() in the SQLite FTS5 extension, fixed upstream in SQLite 3.53.2. Debian fixed it for trixie in sqlite3 3.46.1-7+deb13u2, which backports the upstream fix: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-11822. This owner's first build based on 3.46.1-7+deb13u2 is the fixed version, and its package changelog records the Debian security update for CVE-2026-11822. Earlier builds based on 3.46.1-7+deb13u1 do not carry the fix.
